title: Align arrows on sequence diagram
body: ## :bookmark_tabs: Summary ### Before ### After Resolves #4691 ## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions Instead of changing the complete rendering logic, a check has been added to check if we are not detecting an activation properly. comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I feel like we need to add a JSDoc comment for the `activate` value somewhere (although no functions in this file seem to have any comments).

Does it make sense to do something like:

```js
/**
 * @typedef {Object} AddMessageParams A message from one actor to another.
 * //TODO: add missing types
 * @property {"addMessage"} type - Set to `"addMessage"` if this is an `AddMessageParams`.
 * @property {boolean} [activate] - If `true`, this signal starts an activation.
 */

/**
 * @param {Object | AddMessageParams} param - Object of parameters.
 */
export const apply = function (param) {
```

We don't need to add types/documentation for everything (especially since this is still a JavaScript file, not TypeScript). Just having docs for the new `activate` param that you added is good enough.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment explicitly suggests adding a JSDoc comment for the `activate` parameter, even providing a concrete code example of what it should look like.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: `7.9` seems like a very weird number. I'm guessing this is the number that looks the best, but I just wanted to double-check that you didn't accidentally make a typo.
